headline: The US communications regulator is weighing a request that would let political groups use AI voices in robocalls before the midterms.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: the full AP text supports the headline; the request is still pending.
importance_line: What changed: the FCC is considering a waiver that would let political groups use AI-generated or prerecorded voices in unsolicited calls to cellphones before the November midterm elections. Anyone who gets these calls would be affected if the waiver is granted, and no decision is reported yet.
summary: The Associated Press reports that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), the US communications regulator, is considering a request from a conservative group to loosen rules on political robocalls, including calls with AI-generated voices, before the November midterm elections. US law already forbids most automated calls to mobile phones unless the person agreed in advance, and the group wants an exemption so political campaigns could make such calls with synthetic or recorded voices without that consent.
notes: apnews.com blocked (HTTP 403); AP text read through The Sun Chronicle's AP copy. The conservative group is not named in the text read.
